findings.title: include_website_name conditional missing trailing question mark
findings.body: The method at line 153 is `def include_website_name` (no `?`). ActiveModel::Serializer only recognizes `include_<attr>?` (with the question mark) as a conditional inclusion method; every other `include_*?` method in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_user_fields?`, `include_topic_post_count?`) follows that convention, and the `untrusted_attributes` / `staff_attributes` / `private_attributes` macros at the top of the file all build the method name with `?`. Because the `?` is missing here, AMS treats `website_name` as an attribute that is always serialized: when `user_profile.website` is blank, `json[:website_name]` will appear in the payload with a `nil` value instead of being omitted, and no automated test would catch it because none of the new examples exercise the blank-website case. Rename to `def include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name is not gated by untrusted_attributes and leaks for TL0 users seen by anonymous
findings.body: Line 43 declares `:website_name` as a regular attribute, but the implementation at line 137 derives the value from `user_profile.website`, which is gated for TL0 users via `untrusted_attributes` (see line 109). The TL0/anonymous context in the spec at lines 6–16 was not updated, and the value list at line 11 still does not include `:website_name`. Consequence: for a TL0 user whose `user_profile.website` is set, `website` itself is hidden from anonymous viewers, but the derived `website_name` (which exposes the host and, when the host matches Discourse, the URL path) is still emitted. The current `include_website_name` (without `?`) at line 153 also fails to consult `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (which will generate a properly-named `include_website_name?` that respects the TL0 restriction) instead of keeping a hand-rolled conditional.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed up to three times in website_name
findings.body: Inside `website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is built once for `.host` on line 138 and then twice more for `.path` on lines 143, 146 and 149. Parse the URL once into a local variable and reuse it (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil; return if uri.nil? || uri.host.nil?`), which also makes the method shorter and easier to follow.

findings.title: Domain comparisons are case-sensitive while URI#host is already lowercased
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host` always returns a lowercase host (RFC 3986 §3.2.2), but the comparisons on lines 141, 144, 146 and the `ends_with?` on line 149 compare against `Discourse.current_hostname` verbatim. If an instance is configured with a mixed-case hostname (`Example.com`), a user whose website is `http://example.com/...` will not be recognized as same-domain, so the full path will not be shown even though the two hosts are equivalent per the URL spec. Normalize the instance hostname once (e.g. `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`) or use case-insensitive comparison.

findings.title: TL0 privacy test does not cover website_name and there is no blank-website case
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 (`bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`) was not extended with `:website_name`, so the assertion at lines 13–15 never verifies that `website_name` is excluded for a TL0 user seen by anonymous. There is also no example exercising `website_name` when `user_profile.website` is nil/blank, which is exactly where the `include_website_name` (no `?`) bug at user_serializer.rb:153 would surface — the key would be present with a `nil` value rather than being omitted. Add `website_name` to the untrusted list and add a blank-website expectation.

findings.title: The sibling-subdomain branch in website_name has no test coverage
findings.body: The `elsif` at user_serializer.rb:144–146 (the 'www.example.com / forum.example.com' heuristic that matches sibling subdomains with the same segment count) is reachable but not covered by any of the three new examples. The three added scenarios are (a) completely different domain, (b) identical host, and (c) subdomain via the `ends_with?` else branch — none of them exercises the segment-count branch, so a regression there would not be caught.
